subject: Access controls for customer data — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Access controls for customer data — follow-up and next steps

Laura — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Summary of what we covered:
- Scope: FinTrust will evaluate Redwood for customer-facing features that process limited PII (names, emails, masked account IDs) and telemetry for QA.
- Data residency: Prod instance should be hosted in us-west-2 (AWS). No cross-border replication.
- Retention: Customer-managed retention policy; default token logs retained for 30 days, with a 90-day option.
- Logging & audit: All support activity is logged; break-glass events produce an immutable audit trail with justification and approver.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege roles (admin, ops, support-read, developer). Support access by default is read-only unless break-glass is invoked.

Action items / next steps:
1) I will share our RBAC diagram, role definitions, and a short playbook describing break-glass flow and auditing — attached is the RBAC_diagram.png (see also Drive link).
2) Please send over the specific questions from your security team and the SOC2 evidence request if you have one (we can map items). I attached a blank SOC2_evidence_request.pdf stub we often use.
3) If acceptable, schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive next week with our infra engineer (Dylan) to walk through logs, retention controls, and support procedures.
4) Confirm the primary security contact and a target timeline for review.

Notes / clarifications we promised during call:
- Break-glass: requires a documented justification and a 2-person approval (customer or delegated approver + Redwood on-call for emergency). All break-glass sessions are logged with a before/after snapshot and retained per your retention policy.
- Least privilege: we can pre-provision role templates that mirror your internal roles; onboarding can be via SCIM or manual mapping.

Let me know if you'd like more detail in the RBAC doc before the deep-dive. Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from the FinTrust security team:

1) Break-glass approvals: you mentioned 2-person approval. Will the second approver always be a FinTrust delegate, or can Redwood system admins approve when FinTrust is unreachable? We need to understand escalation boundaries.
2) Audit trail retention: is the break-glass audit retained separately from normal logs, and can we push exports to our SIEM daily?
3) Support access scope: during read-only support sessions do you capture screen-level interactions or just API/log views? We need precise visibility for our compliance team.

We attached our standard security questionnaire to this email (security@fintrust.com). Also, can you confirm whether customer data is ever available to Redwood support personnel in plaintext during debugging?

We can do the technical deep-dive next Tue 12/22 at 10:00 PST if that works for your team.

-Laura

Laura — great questions, answered inline below.

1) Break-glass approvals: By default our policy requires a FinTrust delegate to be one of the approvers for non-emergency access. In emergency situations (defined by an agreed SLA/P1 incident) Redwood on-call can temporarily approve to restore service, but we will always require a post-incident confirmation and audit record from FinTrust. We can include an explicit clause in the mutual action plan if you want that spelled out.

2) Audit retention and SIEM exports: Break-glass audit entries are flagged and retained according to the customer retention policy (separate index). We support daily push of audit logs to your SIEM (S3 delivery or syslog/HTTPS ingestion). We'll include sample log schema in the deep-dive.

3) Support access scope: Support sessions are scoped to API/log views and metadata. We do not surface plaintext customer PII to support by default. For cases where a customer explicitly approves content exposure for debugging, we require documented consent, limited-time access, and a two-person approval flow. All such exposures are logged and can be exported.

We will: attach the RBAC diagram, share role definition table on Drive, and send a short playbook for break-glass flow. Dylan will lead the technical deep-dive on Tue 2026-12-22 at 10:00 PST — invite sent separately.

If you want, we can also provide a redacted example of an audit record for your security team to review.

Best — Marissa

--
